rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: The surah is also called Sabbiḥ; al-Malawi says the Prophet liked it for its abundance of learning and benefits.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سبح قال الملوي : وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبها لكثرة ما اشتملت عليه من العلوم والخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to affirm God's transcendence above every deficiency, including haste, inability to resurrect, purposeless creation, false speech, or speech humans can imitate.
rows.anchor: إيجاب التنزيه للأعلى سبحانه وتعالى عن أن يلحق ساحة عظمته شيء من شوائب النقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah al-Tariq alluded to these denials generally, while this surah explains them in detail.
rows.anchor: كما أذنت بذلك الطارق مجملا وشرحته هذه مفصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as possessing all exaltedness, whose generosity creates, nurtures, and provides for every creature.
rows.anchor: فلا نقص يلحقه { الرحمن } الذي عم جوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy gives His adherents both the obligation and the ability, through guidance, to obey.
rows.anchor: الذي من كان من حزبه فإنه يلزمه الطاعة وييسرها له ويوفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah's call to wait implies that God is free of the defect of haste; its denial that revelation is frivolous answers another accusation.
rows.anchor: بالإمهال النهي عن الاستعجال الذي هو منزه عنه لكونه نقصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands His perfected Messenger to glorify His name because the Messenger alone knows how to do so with full understanding.
rows.anchor: أمر أكمل خلقة رسوله المنزل عليه هذا القرآن صلى الله عليه وسلم بتنزيه اسمه لأنه وحده العالم بذلك حق علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protecting God's name from idolatrous invocation or irreverent use entails even greater reverence for God Himself.
rows.anchor: إذا نزه اسمه عن أن يدعو به وثنا أو غيره أو يضعه في غير ما يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorification, especially declaring God free of impossibilities, comes before affirming attributes; the surah accordingly sets out theology before prophethood.
rows.anchor: شارحا لأصول الدين مقدما للإلهيات التي هي النهايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with God's essence, attributes, self-subsistence, and acts before prophethood cures ignorant imitation and arrogant denial and leads to obedience.
rows.anchor: داء الجهل الموقع في التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabbiḥ means to glorify and clear God with exceptionally strong, emphatic purification.
rows.anchor: أي نزه وبرئ تنزيها وتبرئة عظمتين جدا قويتين شديدتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is the benefactor who creates the person perfectly and raises him through the finest qualities to dignity and beauty.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليك بعد إيجادك على صفة الكمال بتربيتك على أحسن الخلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human well-being needs a powerful patron, an exemplar, and an ideal way; the reported confession names God, Muhammad, and Islam in these roles.
rows.anchor: رضيت بالله ربا وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نبيا ورسولا وبالإسلام دينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿla means supreme in rank, not location, and wholly free of defect, distortive interpretations of His names, or irreverent mention.
rows.anchor: الذي له وصف الأعلوية في المكانة لا المكان على الإطلاق عن كل شائبة نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening glorification formula develops across four forms: the verbal noun in al-Isra, past tense in three surahs, present tense in two, then the imperative here.
rows.anchor: ابتداء سورة الإسراء التي هي سورة الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates from nothing and can bring about whatever He wills without difficulty.
rows.anchor: أي أوجد من العدم أي له صفة الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is followed by proportioning each creature for its perfection and livelihood, balancing conflicting elements through complete knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: أوقع مع الإيجاد وعقبه التسوية في كل خلق بأن جعل له ما يتأتى معه كماله ويتم معاشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balancing of opposed temperaments demonstrates God's wisdom and freely chosen action.
rows.anchor: وذلك بالعلم التام والقدرة الكاملة دلالة على تمام حكمته وفعله بالاختيار

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz defines ḥawa as a horse coat between deep black and dark bay; usage broadened it to mean any black thing.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز رحمه الله في ديوانه : الحوة شية من شيات الخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vegetation may be dark from extreme dryness, swept together by winds and crumbled; the wording combines signs of life and death.
rows.anchor: أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح وجمعته من كل أوب حيت تفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the second descriptor last permits it to carry both its stronger green meaning and the contrasting black meaning.
rows.anchor: وأخر الثانية لتحملها لأن دلالتها على الخضرة أتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The combination of opposites points to one freely acting God; created natural powers have only fixed, necessary effects, like fire that can only burn.
rows.anchor: فدل جمعه بين الأضداد على الذات الواحدة على كمال الاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's recurring beginning and end remind people of resurrection: vegetation becomes dust, then God restores it with water as He restores the dead.
rows.anchor: ثم يعيده سبحانه بالماء على ما كان عليه سواء كما يفعل بالأموات سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pasture is singled out as evidence for resurrection because people cultivate it, and its decay and renewal parallel the dead's restoration.
rows.anchor: وخص المرعى لأنه أدل على البعث لأنه مما ينبته الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's existence, attributes, creative power, guidance, and governance, the surah turns to the creatures and first to the Messenger receiving revelation.
rows.anchor: فدل على تمام أصول الدين بالدلالة على وجوده سبحانه على سبيل التنزل من ذاته إلى صفاته ثم إلى أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human flourishing requires an infallible exemplar; love for God's sake is one of religion's greatest supports.
rows.anchor: ولا مقتدي مثل المعصوم عن كل ميل الموجب ذلك الحب من كل ما يعرف حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeatedly makes the illiterate Prophet a reciter, fully knowledgeable in the life-giving revelation and able to spread and clarify it.
rows.anchor: نجعلك بعظمتنا بوعد لا خلف فيه على سبيل التكرار بالتجديد والاستمرار قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that he will not forget anything ensures both that an unlettered man recites and that his prediction of the future comes true.
rows.anchor: ليكون في ذلك آيتان : كونك تقرأ وأنت أمي , وكونك تخبر عن المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet need not move his tongue hastily or exhaust himself during revelation: God preserves it in his heart and makes his tongue recite it.
rows.anchor: فإن علينا حفظه في صدرك وإنطاق لسانك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns that most people will perish at the upheaval because they prefer fleeting status and wealth to what endures with God.
rows.anchor: إعلام بأن أكثر الخلق يوم الزلزلة هالك لإيثار الفاني من العز والمال على الباقي عند ذي الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath, its object, and what follows disclose this purpose; the title is especially apt because the oath and its answer point to it.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title fits because the oath and its answer point to the surah's purpose.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala presents God as sovereign over all affairs, universally generous in creating and explaining, and specially merciful through guidance to His devoted servants.
rows.anchor: الذي عم بنعمة إيجاده وبيانه فنعمته أتم نعمة وأشمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Zalzalah's account of judgment, this surah traces the disposition that produces evil deeds and the imagined worldly gain that sustains it.
rows.anchor: ختم الزلزلة بالجزاء لأعمال الشر يوم الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath rebukes people who fail to prepare for Judgment, prefer this life to the next, and treat God's blessings without gratitude.
rows.anchor: موبخا من لا يستعد لذلك اليوم بالاحتراز التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Horses are the swift animals meant; their backs bring honor and their bellies wealth, but they earn sin when used for pride and harm and reward when used for God.
rows.anchor: وهي الخيل التي ظهورها عز وبطونها كنز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A horse used in God's cause, with its owner's due care for God's right upon it, becomes a source of protection and reward.
rows.anchor: ومن حمل عليها ولم ينس حق الله في رقابها وظهورها وكانت له سترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath invites reflection on horses' distinctive secrets, which show that their distinguishing features were bestowed by the one sovereign agent; the oath is ultimately by God.
rows.anchor: وإنما أقسم بها ليتأمل ما فيها من الأسرار الكبار التي باينت به أمثالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍabḥ is the loud breathing sound from horses' mouths during intense running, distinct from neighing, snorting, or a camel's bellow.
rows.anchor: والضبح صوت جهير من أفواهها عند العدو الشديد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas renders the horses' ḍabḥ as the sound ah ah, or as running short of a full gallop.
rows.anchor: وحكاه ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فقال : أح أح , أو الضبح عدو دون التقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound was originally associated with foxes and then borrowed for horses; horses, dogs, and foxes are the animals said to make it.
rows.anchor: ليس من الدواب يضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clause names the sparks that galloping produces; the sequencing particle marks the resulting ignition.
rows.anchor: لأن العدو بحيث يتسبب عنه ويتعقبه الإيراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses strike their shoes against stones, especially on rough ground, and thereby cause fire as if forcefully striking flint.
rows.anchor: بما يصطك من نعلها بالأحجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses are credited with the sparks because they cause them, though they do not intend to kindle fire.
rows.anchor: ونسب الإيراء إليها لإيجادها صورته وإن لم يكن لها قصد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses carry their riders into a raid against the enemy, driving hard to kill and plunder.
rows.anchor: الإغارة والركض الشديد لإرادة القتل والنهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A raid is most terrifying when it comes at the end of night.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الإغارة الكائن عنها الثبور والويل أروع ما تكون في أعقاب الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qariʿah depicts the successive moments of Judgment's beginning and outcome and divides people into the saved and the perishing.
rows.anchor: إيضاح يوم الدين بتصوير ثواني أحواله في مبدئه ومآله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Qariʿah clearly expresses the surah's depiction of the Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: واسمها القارعة واضح في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the supreme King, whose creating and explaining benefit all creatures and whose guidance is granted especially to those devoted to Him.
rows.anchor: الذي عمت نعمة إيجاده وبيانه جميع الورى

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading is said to match the reading just mentioned.
rows.anchor: كذلك هي قراءة أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr recited the verse and then said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, during prayer.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير أنه قرأ {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} فقال: سبحان ربي الأعلى وهو في الصلاة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak read it in this manner and instructed anyone who recites it to say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك أنه كان يقرؤها كذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High when he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها قال: سبحان ربي الأعلى

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar would say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High after reciting the verse.
rows.anchor: عن عمر أنه كان إذا قرأ {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} قال: سبحان ربي الأعلى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God guides humans toward happiness or misery and guides livestock to their grazing places.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {والذي قدر فهدى}

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim glosses the pasture as vegetation.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم {والذي أخرج المرعى} قال: النبات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ghutha as dried fragments and ahwa as changed in color.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فجعله غثاء} قال: هشيما {أحوى} قال: متغيرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says ghutha is decayed matter; ahwa is yellow, green, and white before drying after its green stage.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {فجعله غثاء أحوى} قال: الغثاء الشيء البالي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies ghutha as flood debris and ahwa as black.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد {فجعله غثاء أحوى} قال: غثاء السيل و {أحوى} قال: أسود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet reviewed the Quran inwardly because he feared forgetting it, so God assured him that He would suffice him; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستذكر القرآن فخافة أن ينساه فقيل له: كفيناك ذلك

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits a similar report about the Prophet fearing he would forget the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص نحوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The exception means except what God chooses to make the Prophet forget.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس {سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله} يقول إلا ما شئت أنا فأنسيك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed; what God knows as hidden includes whispered thoughts.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله} قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The hidden matters God knows are what a person conceals within himself.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى} قال: ما أخفيت في نفسك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The easy way to which God makes the Prophet ready is goodness.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ونيسرك لليسرى} قال: للخير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Whoever fears God is surely reminded; only the wretched shun the reminder out of disdain for it and its people.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {سيذكر من يخشى ويتجنبها الأشقى} قال: والله ما خشي الله عبد قط إلا ذكره

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet glosses purification as affirming God's oneness, rejecting idols, and testifying that he is God's Messenger; prayer is the five prayers observed at their times.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Purification means freedom from associating partners; remembrance means affirming God's oneness; prayer means the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من الشرك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the successful person is one who says there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى} قال: من قال لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, via Ikrima, likewise interprets purification as saying there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {قد أفلح من تزكى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها إحدى عشرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the surah al-Adiyat was revealed in Mecca.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت و العاديات بمكة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports a Prophetic saying that both al-Zalzalah and al-Adiyat each equal half the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا زلزلت)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas assigns half the Quran to al-Zalzalah and al-Adiyat, a third to al-Ikhlas, and a quarter to al-Kafirun.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا زلزلت) تعدل نصف القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet sent cavalry away for a month without news, and the surah was revealed during their absence.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا فاستمرت شهرا لا يأتيه منها خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses make a ḍabḥ with their feet; Ibn Mardawayh's wording instead says they snort through their nostrils.
rows.anchor: ضحت بأرجلها ولفظ ابن مردويه ضبحت بمناخيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hooves strike stones and kindle sparks.
rows.anchor: قدحت بحوافرها الحجارة فأورت نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attack the enemy in the morning.
rows.anchor: صبحت القوم بغارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hooves raise dust from the ground.
rows.anchor: أثارت بحوافرها التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reach the midst of the enemy's group.
rows.anchor: صبحت القوم جميعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the episode as an expedition whose delayed report troubled the Prophet; God informed him of its progress and outcome.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى العدو فأبطأ خبرها فشق ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The horses' ḍabḥ is their snorting while racing.
rows.anchor: قال: هي الخيل والضبح: نخير الخيل حتى تنخر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The horses spark fire with their hoofs as they run over stone.
rows.anchor: قال: حين تجري الخيل توري نارا أصابت بسنابكها الحجارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The cavalry raids and surprises the enemy in the morning.
rows.anchor: قال: هي الخيل أغارت فصبحت العدو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The horses raise dust with their hooves as they run.
rows.anchor: قال: هي الخيل أثرن بحوافرها يقول تعدو الخيل والنقع الغبار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The group reached by the horses is the enemy.
rows.anchor: قال: الجمع العدو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the horses in battle lower their lips as they prepare to race, and that sparks expose the pagans' stratagem.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس هي الخيل في القتال وضبحها حين ترخي مشافرها إذا أعدت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The attack occurs when the horses reach the enemy in the morning and penetrate their ranks.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس هي الخيل في القتال وضبحها حين ترخي مشافرها إذا أعدت

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih insists that Ali interpreted the oath as pilgrimage camels and says his own patron was more knowledgeable than Ikrima's.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح: فقلت: قال علي: هي الإبل في الحج ومولاي كان أعلم من مولاك

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali rejects the cavalry reading because early Badr had only the reported horses; he identifies the oath with pilgrims' camels running from Arafat through Muzdalifa, where they kindle fires.
rows.anchor: والله إن أول غزوة في الإسلام لبدر وما كان معنا إلا فرسان للزبير وفرس للمقداد بن الأسود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet would rehearse the Quran to himself because he feared forgetting it.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : سنقرئك فلا تنسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The exception means what God wills to make the Prophet forget.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس سنقرئك فلا تنسى الا ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked about the oath, Ibn Abbas first says it means horses raiding for God and resting at night; Ali objects that Badr had only a few horses and says the camels run from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina, raising dust and reaching Jam. Ibn Abbas recants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah (Ibn Masʿud) interprets the oath as camels.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله والعاديات ضبحا قال : الابل

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports Ali's interpretation as camels and says Ibn Abbas connected the verse to a dispatched expedition.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم : وقال علي بن أبي طالب : هي الابل وقال ابن عباس : إنما كان ذلك في سرية بعثت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says only dogs and horses among animals make a ḍabḥ.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والعاديات ضبحا قال : ليس بشيء من الدواب يضبح الا كلب أو فرس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sparks as a man's stratagem with a flint that produces a spark.
rows.anchor: فالموريات قدحا قال : هو مكر الرجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says horses raid at dawn, kick up dust from their hoof marks, and reach the enemy group.
rows.anchor: فالمغيرات صبحا قال : غارت الخيل صبحا فأثرن به نقعا قال : غبار وقع سنابك الخيل

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr used to identify the oath animals as camels.
rows.anchor: عبيد بن عمير يقول : هي الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has nineteen verses by unanimous agreement among the verse counters.
rows.anchor: وعدد آيها تسع عشرة آية باتفاق أهل العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its purposes include glorifying God and indicating His oneness through His unique creation of humans and earthly sustenance.
rows.anchor: تنزيه الله تعالى والإشارة إلى وحدانيته لانفراده بخلق الإنسان وخلق ما في الأرض مما فيه بقاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah supports and steadies the Prophet in receiving revelation and promises him a gracious law and a book that reminds the purified and God-fearing.
rows.anchor: شريعة سمحة وكتابا يتذكر به أهل النفوس الزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pure and fearful heed the reminder, while the wretched prefer worldly life and disregard the eternal one.
rows.anchor: يتذكر به أهل النفوس الزكية الذين يخشون ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation confirms earlier messengers' scriptures and thus comforts the Prophet amid pagan rejection.
rows.anchor: وأن ما أوحي إليه يصدقه ما في كتب الرسل من قبله وذلك كله تهوين لما يلقاه من إعراض المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reproductive powers suited to animal life and preservation of species are among the clearest instances of divine ordaining and guidance.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل مظاهر التقدير والهداية تقدير قوى التناسل للحيوان لبقاء النوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of guided is omitted for generality, then restricted to beings capable of guidance: animals with perception and will, not fruiting or seed-producing plants.
rows.anchor: محذوف لإفادة العموم وهو عام مخصوص بما فيه قابلية الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proportioning and guidance suit the surah because God who fashioned the Prophet for the burdens of mission also equips him to retain revelation and grants him an easy law.
rows.anchor: الذي يسوي خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسوية تلائم ما خلقه لأجله من تحمل أعباء الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's swift change from growth to chaff embeds a reminder of death after life, as in the human progression from weakness to strength and back.
rows.anchor: إدماج العبرة بتصاريف ما أودع الله في المخلوقات من مختلف الأطوار من الشيء إلى ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition particle suggests the brief span between verdant growth and chaff, like worldly vegetation that quickly becomes a vanished harvest.
rows.anchor: الحرف الموضوع لعطف ما يحصل فيه حكم المعطوف بعد زمن قريب من زمن حصول المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening command to glorify was general glad tidings; this passage makes explicit the promise to preserve every recited revelation for full delivery.
rows.anchor: فهذا موقع البيان الصريح بوعده بأنه سيعصمه من نسيان ما يقرئه فيبلغه كما أوحي إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An authentic report says the Prophet struggled to retain revelation, moved his lips while Gabriel recited, and later recited it exactly as Gabriel had.
rows.anchor: في الصحيح عن ابن عباس : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعالج من التنزيل شدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the linked passage in al-Qiyamah was revealed later, this verse is an earlier promise that God will help the Prophet preserve all revelation.
rows.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى فقد تعين أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of recitation prepares for the central promise that the Prophet will not forget and assures him that preservation will continue as the Quran grows.
rows.anchor: إدماجا للإعلام بأن القرآن في تزايد مستمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future marker sin confirms a coming act and, alongside an act already underway, signals that recitation will continue and renew.
rows.anchor: فالسين دالة على أن الإقراء يستمر ويتجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to God's majestic first-person plural suits His direct approach to the Prophet with glad tidings.
rows.anchor: والالتفات بضمير المتكلم المعظم لأن التكلم أنسب بالإقبال على المبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing recitation to God is a rational attribution: He creates the words being recited and commands their recitation.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الإقراء إلى الله مجاز عقلي لأنه جاعل الكلام المقروء وآمر بإقرائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet will not forget is declarative in form but functions as a promise and guarantee.
rows.anchor: خبر مراد به الوعد والتكفل له بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means whatever God chooses for the Prophet to forget; the object of chooses is omitted in keeping with common Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا ما شاء الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first and most evident case is abrogation of recitation: God has the Prophet and community stop reciting material until they forget it.
rows.anchor: أن الله إذا شاء نسخ تلاوة بعض ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمره بأن يترك قراءته

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar reports that the revealed material once included a stoning verse and a warning against disowning one's fathers.
rows.anchor: مثل ما روي عن عمر أنه قال : ( كان فيما أنزل الشيخ والشيخه إذا زنيا فارجموهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second case is temporary human lapse, after which God provides a reminder.
rows.anchor: نسيانا موقتا كشأن عوارض الحافظة البشرية ثم يقيض الله له ما يذكره به

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that a man reciting at night reminded the Prophet of verses he had omitted or forgotten; on another occasion Ubayy asked whether a verse omitted in prayer had been abrogated, and the Prophet said he had forgotten.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : ( سمع النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقرأ من الليل بالمسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is not a prohibition: forgetting is not subject to obligation, and treating the particle as prohibitive to explain its written alif is strained.
rows.anchor: ليس قوله : { فلا تنسى } من الخبر المستعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God knows what is manifest and hidden is an interruption explaining His guarantee: public recitation is manifest, while omitted forgotten recitation is hidden.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة الجهر وما يخفى أن ما يقرؤه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن هو من قبيل الجهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ease promised to the Prophet broadens the preceding promise of preservation: it means making good easy for him, not simply protecting revelation.
rows.anchor: مفهومها الحفظ والصيانة ومفهوم المعطوفة تيسير الخير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taysir means making a task easy for its doer, with the benefited person commonly expressed by a following phrase with li-.
rows.anchor: والتيسير : جعل العمل يسيرا على عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusra is the feminine of al-aysar, and the faʿla pattern intensifies the quality.
rows.anchor: واليسرى : مؤنث الأيسر ، وصيغة فعلى تدل على قوة الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early Qayrawan, Tunisian, and eastern codices and some commentaries call it al-Adiyat without waw; other tafsirs retain the opening waw in the title.
rows.anchor: سميت في المصاحف القيروانية العتيقة والتونسية والمشرقية ( سورة العاديات ) بدون واو

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ata, al-Hasan, and Ikrima classify the surah as Meccan.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وجابر بن زيد وعطاء والحسن وعكرمة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Abbas, and Qatada classify the surah as Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وقتادة : هي مدنية

rows.speaker: جابر بن زيد
rows.claim: On the Meccan classification, Jabir ibn Zayd ranks it fourteenth in revelation order, after al-Asr and before al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: وعدت الرابعة عشرة في ترتيب نزول السور عند جابر بن زيد بناء على أنها مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: وآيها إحدى عشرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi attributes to Muqatil and others a report that a cavalry force sent against Banu Kinana was delayed for a month, rumors said they had died, and the verses announced their deeds.
rows.anchor: ذكر الواحدي في ( أسباب النزول ) عن مقاتل وعن غيره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث خيلا سرية

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the Bazzar version of the expedition report very strange.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير : روى أبو بكر البزار هنا حديثا غريبا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite its strangeness, the report could be accepted, but its chain contains the weak Hafs ibn Jamiʿ; the stronger view is that the surah is Medinan.
rows.anchor: إلا أن في سنده حفص بن جميع وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah condemns traits leading to loss in the afterlife, especially prevalent among pagans and hypocrites, and warns Muslims against them.
rows.anchor: ذم خصال تفضي بأصحابها إلى الخسران في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It reminds people that their deeds will be judged after death, reassuring believers and threatening deniers; the opening oath also honors warhorses or pilgrimage mounts.
rows.anchor: ووعظ الناس بأن وراءهم حسابا على أعمالهم بعد الموت ليتذكره المؤمن ويهدد به الجاحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Adiyat is the active participle of running quickly, used especially for horses and camels, and by analogy for renowned human runners.
rows.anchor: جمع العادية ، وهو اسم فاعل من العدو وهو السير السريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four Arab runners were proverbial: al-Sulayk ibn al-Salka, al-Shanfara, Taʾabbata Sharran, and Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri.
rows.anchor: السليك بن السلكة ، والشنفرى ، وتأبط شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form agrees with its non-rational referent.
rows.anchor: وتأنيث هذا الوصف هنا لأنه من صفات ما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍabḥ is breath vibrating in the throat without leaving the mouth, a sound made by horses and predatory animals.
rows.anchor: والضبح : اضطراب النفس المتردد في الحنجرة دون أن يخرج من الفم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas demonstrates ḍabḥ by imitating the sound ah ah.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء : سمعت ابن عباس يصف الضبح أح أح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no animal besides a horse, dog, or fox makes a ḍabḥ; the lexicographers also report this view.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ليس شيء من الدواب يضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas first identified the oath with horses raiding for God; Ali argued Badr had only two horses and instead identified pilgrimage camels traveling from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina, so Ibn Abbas withdrew his answer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali's words do not explicitly classify the surah as Meccan or Medinan; Ibn Masʿud, Ibrahim, Mujahid, and Ubayd ibn Umayr give the same camel interpretation.
rows.anchor: وليس في قول علي رضي الله عنه تصريح بأنها مكية ولا مدنية وبمثل ما قال علي قال ابن مسعود وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguists do not use ḍabḥ for camel sounds; on a camel reading, al-Mubarrad and others interpret it as ḍabʿ, extending the forelegs while running.
rows.anchor: والضبح لا يطلق على صوت الإبل في قول أهل اللغة .

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says horses may also be described by the related verb for extending their forelegs when running, with ḍabḥ a dialect form replacing ʿayn with ḥaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : ضبحت الخيل وضبعت

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf rejects the proposed letter interchange as unsupported, though al-Qamus adopts it.
rows.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( وليس بثبت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With camels, ḍabḥ can be a metaphor for their intensified running sound, or a dialectal substitution for ḍabʿ.
rows.anchor: يكون الضبح استعير لصوت الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍabḥan may be an accusative circumstantial expression of their sound, or describe the manner of running if derived from ḍabʿ.
rows.anchor: إذا أريد به الصوت الذي يتردد في جوفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the oath concerns pilgrimage camels, it honors animals whose service is esteemed by both pagans and Muslims, making the sworn claim persuasive to all.
rows.anchor: واختير القسم بها لأن السامعين يوقنون أن ما يقسم عليه بها محقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muriyat are those that kindle; qadh is striking one surface against another to make a spark, and qadhan is an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والموريات : التي توري ، أي توقد

rows.speaker: الشنفرى
rows.claim: Al-Shanfara's line compares his running to a camel whose hooves make sparks from flint, illustrating extreme speed.
rows.anchor: إذا الأمعز الصوان لاقى مناسمي تطاير منه قادح ومفلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sparks could be fires lit at night for needs and food, or a metaphor for stirring war, as war is likened to a fire.
rows.anchor: مستعار لإثارة الحرب لأن الحرب تشبه بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadh could instead mean drawing broth from a cooking pot into serving bowls for an army or caravan; here it would express purpose.
rows.anchor: بمعنى استخراج المرق من القدر في القداح لإطعام الجيش أو الركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mughirat derives from raid; attributing the riders' raiding to their mounts is a rational trope because horses or camels are its means, though it can also mean rushing along.
rows.anchor: والمغيرات : اسم فاعل من أغار ، والإغارة تطلق على غزو الجيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For warhorses, the raid occurs at dawn because raids began after daybreak, prompting the warning cry ya sabahah.
rows.anchor: فتقييد ذلك بوقت الصبح لأنهم كانوا إذا غزوا لا يغيرون على القوم إلا بعد الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For racing pilgrimage camels, the phrase means departing Muzdalifa for Mina on the morning of the sacrifice, as the sun rose over Thabir.
rows.anchor: فالمراد : دفعها من مزدلفة إلى منى صباح يوم النحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying 'Rise, Thabir, so we may depart' refers to that pilgrimage movement.
rows.anchor: ومن أقوالهم في ذلك : ( أشرق ثبير كيما نغير )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The runners excite dust from the ground through the force of their gallop; naqʿ means dust.
rows.anchor: الإثارة : الإهاجة ، والنقع : الغبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi can mark cause, with its pronoun referring to running, or location, referring to the morning when they raided.
rows.anchor: والباء في { به } يجوز أن تكون سببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasatna means to be in the middle of a group; for warhorses, the group is the enemy they surround.
rows.anchor: كن وسط الجمع ، يقال : وسط القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For pilgrimage camels, jamʿ denotes the place Muzdalifa, since the phrase describes their arrival there rather than a settled crowd.
rows.anchor: فأما بالنسبة إلى الإبل فيتعين أن يكون قوله : { جمعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The carefully chosen words accommodate both warhorses and pilgrimage camels, a feature of the surah's rhetorical arrangement.
rows.anchor: ومن بديع النظم وإعجازه إيثار كلمات ( العاديات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabbiḥ means glorify and sanctify God, declaring Him free of defects, other gods, and the claims of polytheists.
rows.anchor: بمعنى نزه وقدس وقل سبحانه عن النقائص والغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ism can refer to its bearer, making it virtually redundant here, or to the act and form of naming itself.
rows.anchor: يراد به المسمى، ويأتي في مواضع يراد به التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean glorify the Lord Himself, or protect His name from being applied to an idol; al-Aʿla may modify either the name or the Lord.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تحتمل هذا الوجه الأول، وتحتمل أن يراد بالاسم التسمية نفسها

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: According to al-Tabari, Ibn Umar and Ali read the verse as Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, as in Ubayy's codex.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن ابن عمر وعليا قرآ هذه السورة: «سبحان ربي الأعلى»

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashari, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Malik ibn Dinar are also reported to read it as Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير ومالك بن أبي دينار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High upon reciting the verse.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the command means to mention God's name only while reverent and humble.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى سبح اسم ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as pray in the name of your Lord, with the preposition omitted as in begin in God's name.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس معنى الآية: صل باسم ربك الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwa means proportioned and perfected creation so its order displays God's power and oneness.
rows.anchor: معناه عدل وأتقن حتى صارت الأمور مستوية دالة على قدرته ووحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled d; it can mean decree or determine by measure.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «قدر» بشد الدال فيحتمل أن يكون من القدر والقضاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses guidance as both guiding and leading astray, with the stated half implying its counterpart.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: معناه هدى وأضل، واكتفى بالواحدة لدلالتها على الأخرى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God guides animals to mating.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: هدى الحيوان إلى وطء الذكور الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God guides a newborn, upon delivery, to suckle at the breast.
rows.anchor: وقيل هدى المولود عند وضعه إلى مص الثدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says people are guided to good or evil and livestock to their grazing places.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هدى الناس للخير والشر، والبهائم للمراتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These interpretations are examples; the soundest reading keeps the verse general across kinds of ordaining and guidance.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذه الأقوال مثالات، والعموم في الآية أصوب في كل تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-marʿa is vegetation, the basis of livelihood because livestock eat it and people also benefit from it.
rows.anchor: والمرعى: النبات، وهو أصل في قيام المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghutha is dried, brittle vegetation carried by floodwater and can describe people of little worth.
rows.anchor: ما يبس وجف وتحطم من النبات، وهو الذي يحمله السيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahwa may mean dark green from lushness or black tinged with green, as in Dhu al-Rumma's description of dark lips.
rows.anchor: قيل هو الأخضر الذي عليه سواد من شدة الخضرة والغضارة، وقيل هو الأسود سوادا يضرب إلى الخضرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada construes the syntax as God bringing out luxuriantly dark-green pasture, then making it chaff when it dries; ahwa is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: تقدير هذه الآية أخرج المرعى، أحوى أسود من خضرته ونضارته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the old chaff becomes black and rotten after rain, explaining ghutha ahwa as black.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى فجعله غثاء أحوى أي أسود، لأن الغثاء إذا قدم وأصابته الأمطار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and Malik ibn Anas connect the promise not to forget with the instruction in al-Qiyamah not to move the tongue hastily.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة ومالك بن أنس: هذه الآية في معنى قوله تعالى: لا تحرك به لسانك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Amir, and Ibn al-Zubayr also used to say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود وابن عامر وابن الزبير يفعلون ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed believers to include its glorification in prostration.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اجعلوها في سجودكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others distinguish this verse from al-Qiyamah: it promises that the Prophet will retain the revealed law and surahs and reinforces his duty to keep them in mind.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: ليست هذه الآية في معنى تلك، وإنما هذه وعد بإقرار الشرع والسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final ya in tansā is written to match the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وأثبت الياء في «تنسى» لتعديل رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd interprets not forgetting as not abandoning the commands and prohibitions in revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد: معنى فلا تنسى، لا تترك العمل بما تضمن من أمر ونهي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others say the exception concerns material whose recitation and legal ruling God abrogates.
rows.anchor: الحسن وقتادة وغيره مما قضى الله تعالى بنسخه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra and other linguists regard the exception as a conventional parenthetical expression, with nothing actually permitted to be forgotten.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة من أهل المعاني: هو استثناء صلة في الكلام على سنة الله تعالى في الاستثناء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God may make the Prophet forget something so he can establish a Sunnah, as in the saying I forget or am made to forget for that purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيكه لتسن به على نحو قوله عليه السلام: «إني لأنسى أو أنسى لأسن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes say God may let the Prophet forget temporarily and then remind him, as happened when another man's recitation reminded him of verses.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين: إلا ما شاء الله أن يغلبك النسيان عليه ثم يذكرك به بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For what he is commanded to convey, the Prophet is protected from forgetting; after learning it he may forget and later recall it, establish a Sunnah, or experience abrogation.
rows.anchor: ونسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممتنع فيما أمر بتبليغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge encompasses manifest and hidden things, validating the report that He reminds the Prophet of what he has forgotten.
rows.anchor: لإحاطته بكل شيء علما، وبهذا يصح الخبر بأنه لا ينسى شيئا إلا ذكره الله تعالى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God directs the Prophet toward good things in this life and the next: victory, success, the elevation of his message, and high rank in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ونيسرك لليسرى معناه: نذهب بك نحو الأمور المستحسنة في دنياك وأخراك من النصر والظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to preserve revelation so the unlettered Prophet does not lose it; this is a sign of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وعد الله أن يقرئه وأخبره أنه لا ينسى نسيانا لا يكون بعده ذكر، فتذهب الآية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zuhrawi interpret if the reminder benefits as even if it does not, since one condition implies its opposite.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء والزهراوي معناه: وإن لم تنفع، فاقتصر على القسم الواحد لدلالته على الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some rhetoricians take the phrase as an aside reproaching Quraysh: would a reminder benefit these defiant people?
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الحذاق: إنما قوله إن نفعت الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem illustrates this reproach: one has spoken to the living, but the addressee is unresponsive as if lifeless.
rows.anchor: لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حيا ... ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God and the Hereafter will heed the reminder, while the one destined for misery rejects it and faces the Fire.
rows.anchor: سيذكر من يخشى الله والدار الآخرة، وهم العلماء والمؤمنون كل بقدر ما وفق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the great Fire is the Fire of the Hereafter, while the lesser one is the fire of this world.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: النار الكبرى نار الآخرة، والصغرى نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the Hereafter's Fire itself has degrees, with some portions greater than others.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: إن نار جميع الآخرة وإن كانت شديدة فهي تتفاضل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra identifies the great Fire as the lowest of Hell's levels.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الكبرى هي السفلى من أطباق النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not dying and not living means no relieving death and no pleasant life; the condemned remain alive, though a report calls sinners in Hell dead metaphorically.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيها موتا مريحا، ولا يحيى حياة هنية فهو لا محالة حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that sinners are dead in Hell is figurative, describing a state like dormancy, stillness, or languishing.
rows.anchor: وأراه على التشبيه لأنه كالسبات والركود والهمول فجعله موتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, and Ikrima identify the oath animals as horses running with their riders and making a sound; an expedition to Banu Kinana may have occasioned the surah.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة: أراد الخيل لأنها تعدو بالفرسان وتصيح بأصواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the oath as horses generally, whose speed and strength have long made them conquer lands and kingdoms; good remains in their forelocks.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: القسم هو بالخيل جملة لأنها تعدو ضابحة قديما وحديثا

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ibrahim, and Ubayd ibn Umayr say the animals are camels, which make a ḍabḥ while running; Ali includes pilgrims' and Badr's camels.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وإبراهيم وعبيد بن عمير: العاديات في هذه الآية: الإبل

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the oath refers to pilgrims' camels running between Arafat and Muzdalifa, as well as Badr's camels, since that battle had very few horses.
rows.anchor: قال علي: والقسم بالإبل العاديات من عرفة ومن مزدلفة إذا وقع الحاج وبإبل غزوة بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍabḥ is a loud sound during intense running, distinct from neighing, roaring, and barking; it is an unusual animal sound.
rows.anchor: والضبح: تصويت جهير عند العدو الشديد ليس بصهيل ولا رغاء ولا نباح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that only horses and dogs make a ḍabḥ; the author rejects this as unsound because Arabs also apply the word to camels, snakes, owls, rabbits, foxes, echoes, and bows.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال: ليس يضبح من الحيوان غير الخيل والكلاب

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's verse about a bow making a fox-like ḍabḥ in the hand supports the word's broader use beyond horses and dogs.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو حنيفة في صفة قوس: [الرجز] حنانة من نشم أو تالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may concern warhorses, pilgrimage camels, or both.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في الآية، أن القسم بالخيل أو بالإبل أو بهما

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Masʿud say the camels spark fire as stones they kick strike one another.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود: هي الإبل، وذلك أنها في عدوها ترجم الحصى بالحصى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the sparks as those made by horses' hooves striking stones.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي الخيل، وذلك بحوافرها في الحجارة

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl defines the ungrateful person as one whose single sin makes him forget many good deeds and who treats God as if owed a return.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضيل: الكنود الذي تنسيه سيئة واحدة حسنات كثيرة ويعامل الله على عقد عوض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the witness to human ingratitude is God, who witnesses against the person.
rows.anchor: أي وربه شاهد عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan and Mujahid take the witness to be the person himself: his actions, words, and known character testify against him.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن ومجاهد، والضمير في قوله تعالى: وإنه لحب الخير عائد على «الإنسان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the love-of-good clause refers to the human being; because of love for wealth he is intensely miserly and guards it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى من أجل حب الخير إنه لشديد، أي بخيل بالمال ضابط له

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says that wherever good appears in the Quran it means wealth.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: الخير حيث وقع في القرآن فهو المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here good may mean worldly wealth, health, and status, which disbelievers and the ignorant value; loving the good of the Hereafter is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد هنا الخير الدنياوي من مال وصحة وجاه عند الملوك ونحوه

rows.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
rows.claim: Tarafa's verse about death selecting a miser's precious wealth illustrates the meaning of a person who hoards it.
rows.anchor: أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي ... عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question challenges the person about wealth and final destiny: does he not know his destination and prepare for it?
rows.anchor: أفلا يعلم مآله فيستعد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿthara means exposing what is hidden in graves by searching and uncovering it.
rows.anchor: تقصيه مما يستره والبحث عنه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's codex reads search in place of baʿthara.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود: «بحث ما في القبور»

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading gives the graves as searched and exposed.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي: «وبحثرت القبور» ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gathering what lies in hearts means distinguishing and exposing faith, disbelief, and intention so each can be recompensed.
rows.anchor: تمييزه وكشفه ليقع الجزاء عليه من إيمان وكفر ونية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying that people will be raised according to their intentions explains the exposure of what is in hearts.
rows.anchor: ويفسره قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يبعث الناس يوم القيامة على نياتهم»

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar and Nasr ibn Asim read the word for bringing forth with fatḥa on both ḥa and ṣad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر ونصر بن عاصم: بفتح الحاء والصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of people is stated as a firm truthful assertion and singled out for Judgment Day because it is the day of requital and an explicit threat.
rows.anchor: لكن خصص يومئذ لأنه يوم المجازاة، فإليه طمحت النفوس، وهذا وعيد مصرح

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God will teach the Prophet the Quran and gather it in his heart so that he will never forget it.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل سنعلمك القرآن ونجمعه في قلبك فلا تنساه أبدا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: One view identifies the oath as pilgrimage camels, held by Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayd ibn Umayr, al-Qurazi, and al-Suddi; Ali says they run from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها الإبل في الحج قاله علي وابن مسعود وعبيد بن عمير والقرظي والسدي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali describes Badr, saying the Muslims then had only one horse, though another report gives two.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي أنه قال هذا في صفة وقعة بدر قال وما كان معنا يومئذ إلا فرس وفي بعض الحديث أنه كان معهم فرسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The other view identifies the oath as horses campaigning for God; it is attributed to Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Ata, Mujahid, and other early authorities and linguists.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها الخيل في سبيل الله قاله ابن عباس والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas understood the horses to be from an expedition sent by the Prophet whose news was delayed for a month.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يذهب إلى أن هذا كان في سرية فروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله بعث خيلا فلم يأته خبرها شهرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the expedition account, the horses snort through their nostrils, spark with their hooves on stones, attack at dawn, raise dust, and reach the enemy together.
rows.anchor: ضبحت بمناخرها فالموريات قدحا قدحت بحوافرها الحجارة فأورت نارا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says a force sent to two Banu Kinana clans under al-Mundhir ibn Amr was delayed; rumors by Jews and hypocrites made Muslims fear their relatives had died.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى حيين من كنانة واستعمل عليها المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The surah was revealed to report how the expedition had fared and to allay the fear stirred by the rumors.
rows.anchor: فنزلت والعاديات ضبحا فأخبر الله كيف فعل بهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra defines ḍabḥ as the sound of horses' breaths when they run.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء الضبح أصوات أنفاس الخيل إذا عدون

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says ḍabḥ is the sound in horses' throats when they run.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة الضبح صوت حلوقها إذا عدت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ḍabḥ is the sound of the horses' insides when they run.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج ضبحها صوت أجوافها إذا عدت
